overview: This Senate resolution names June 10, 2025, as 'DACOR Bacon House Bicentennial Day' to mark 200 years since the DACOR Bacon House was completed in Washington, D.C. The house, a few blocks from the White House, was home over the years to Supreme Court justices, members of Congress, and a Russian diplomat, and was built in part by enslaved people. Since 1986 it has been the headquarters of Diplomatic and Consular Officers, Retired (DACOR), an organization of current and former foreign affairs professionals. The resolution recognizes the house's place in the history of diplomacy, the Supreme Court, and Congress, and applauds the groups that preserve it. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 17, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution recognizes a historic landmark tied to two centuries of American government and diplomacy, and the people who have worked to preserve it.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
